During the winter of 2021, 2022, the City of Saskatoon Transit experience significant disruptions.
The primary reasons for the disruptions communicated to the public were extreme weather conditions.
Global part shortage and the age of the bus fleet.
In April 2022, the City Council asked the independent office of the City Auditor to investigate the service disruptions.
The objective of the investigation was to conduct a root cause analysis of service disruptions and provide cost effective and practical recommendations.
To avoid future disruptions in Saskatoon Transit.
The areas covered within the investigation were sourcing of parts, preventive maintenance and repairs, communication and reporting,
age of the bus fleet and resources.
As part of the investigation, the investigation team met with the various staff and other stakeholders including the ATU and the bus riders of Saskatoon.
The investigation was evidence-based and the team conducted a detailed review of documents and records to conclude the reasons for the service disruption.
The findings and recommendations were shared with the administration throughout the investigation to ensure there is lead time for fixing immediate issues before the winter.
The investigation concluded that multifaceted factors resulted in service disruption.
In effective stores operations was the first main reason that resulted in delays in providing parts required for buses.
We noted that staffing levels at the stores were inadequate.
Inventory management was ineffective.
Manual processes were used for procurement of parts and inadequate support was provided to store staff in using the new system.
In effective governance was a second main reason for service disruption.
We noted that management of transit issues were not well managed.
There was lack of stakeholder engagement.
Performance indicators were non-existent for bus repairs.
There was lack of timely and accurate data for decision making and communication processes were ineffective.
In effective preventive maintenance program was a third main reason for the disruption of transit services.
60% of the buses did not receive timely preventive maintenance during the last two years, which resulted in more work curing a winter when a breakdown occurred or increased likelihood of breakdowns.
Key recommendations arising from the investigation include,
Stranding the stores operations which includes string lining inventory management, enhancing support to store staff in using the new system and implementing policies and procedures.
Improving the governance processes by increasing management presence, implementing measures to increase spare buses,
Building strong stakeholder relationships, obtaining accurate and timely data for informed decision making,
Improving supervisor to staff ratio and expediting the recruitment for director of transit.
Ensuring that preventive maintenance is conducted in accordance with the maintenance schedule.
Carefully analyzing the information before making a public disclosure to ensure accuracy,
Implementing formal communication timelines for reporting service disruptions to the public and ensuring that adequate lead time is provided to riders to allow for alternative travel plans.
And finally conducting a workplace culture audit at transit and implementing strategies to improve the workplace culture.

The independent office of the city auditor will obtain regular status updates from administration on the implementation of the recommendations and will conduct a follow up to assess whether these recommendations are effectively implemented.
A follow-up report will be provided to the committee in Q3 of 2020-23.
